title: Applying critical energy and testing spin-colour channels
question: how does the critical energy theorem close the earlier programme, and can spin or colour supply its missing estimate?

verdict.conclusion: If the critical dyadic Chebyshev-energy estimate were proved, it would close the arithmetic controller, force RH, set every seam defect and horizontal residue to zero, and identify the ordinate and exact Weil channels. Spin and colour do not presently prove that estimate. As internal SU(2)xSU(3) degeneracy they leave the scalar singlet and coefficient radius unchanged; as six spectral descendants they exceed the four-branch seam-contraction theorem and can expand the defect at small displacement.

spinColourStateSpace.spinRepresentation: V_spin=C^2, fundamental SU(2) doublet with two spin projections
spinColourStateSpace.colourRepresentation: V_colour=C^3, fundamental SU(3) triplet with three colours
spinColourStateSpace.operatorDecomposition: End(V)=(1,1) plus (3,1) plus (1,8) plus (3,8), with dimensions 1+3+8+24=36
spinColourStateSpace.scalarVisibility: a normalized colour- and spin-blind trace sees only the (1,1) singlet; Pauli and colour generators are traceless
spinColourStateSpace.existingTernaryRelation: the earlier Z_3 phase model can at most represent the center/triality shadow of SU(3); Z_3 alone does not derive the full eight-generator colour gauge symmetry
spinColourStateSpace.existingQuaternaryRelation: the earlier four-state alternatives do not derive spin: SU(2) has a two-dimensional fundamental representation and center Z_2, while a four-state scalar model needs an independently specified tensor product or coupling

singletBottleneck.candidateMatrixTheorem: for every delta>0, integral_X^(2X)||Psi_matrix(x)-x I_6||_HS^2 dx is O_delta(X^(2+delta))
singletBottleneck.consequence: the matrix theorem implies the scalar critical energy theorem
singletBottleneck.difficulty: it is stronger, not weaker: nonsinglet spin-colour channels add nonnegative energy and cannot cancel the scalar singlet norm

spinPhaseAndSupertrace.unitaryPhase: spin or colour phases disappear from absolute-square Hilbert energy
spinPhaseAndSupertrace.orthogonalChannels: energies add by Pythagoras rather than cancel
spinPhaseAndSupertrace.supertrace: a signed boson-fermion supertrace could cancel amplitudes, but it is indefinite and does not provide the positive L2 norm needed for the Mellin Cauchy-Schwarz argument

seamMultiplicityAudit.internalDegeneracyReading: if all d internal states remain attached to one spectral zero before and after halving, the common factor d cancels from the comparison and the defect contracts
seamMultiplicityAudit.spectralDescendantReading: if one parent zero creates six distinct half-displacement zeros, compare epsilon(eta) with 6epsilon(eta/2)
seamMultiplicityAudit.interpretation: six half-displacement descendants expand the defect for 0<|eta|<about 0.424141 and contract only above that threshold
